content: In 2012, the World Health Organization (WHO) initiated the development of a guideline to determine optimal serum and red blood cell folate concentrations in women of reproductive age to prevent neural tube defects (NTDs). This effort involved representatives from all WHO departments and was guided by a steering committee that oversaw the entire process. Two additional groups were formed: an advisory guideline group and an external review group. The guideline development group, established specifically for this project, included experts from various WHO advisory panels and specialists identified through open calls. The guideline development group advised WHO on selecting critical outcomes for decision-making and interpreting evidence. Participants included content experts, methodologists, health professionals involved in nutrition surveillance, and technical staff from WHO and health ministries. Representatives from commercial organizations were excluded from membership. External reviewers were identified through WHO’s nutrition mailing lists and website, ensuring proper interpretation of recommendations. Three content experts peer-reviewed the draft guideline and provided technical input. The guideline’s scope and evidence appraisal began with drafting key questions by WHO’s Evidence and Programme Guidance Unit, based on the needs of member states. The methodological approach for retrieving, summarizing, and assessing evidence on folate status and NTD risk was discussed with stakeholders. A formal meeting of the guideline development group was held in Geneva in September 2013, where systematic reviews and GRADE evidence profiles were used to draft recommendations. The group reached consensus on the recommendations, considering evidence quality, intervention effects, feasibility, and costs. Conflict of interest management followed WHO’s strict guidelines. All participants declared potential conflicts of interest before meetings, and these were reviewed by WHO technical officers. Participants acted in their individual capacities, not as institutional representatives. Experts with relevant intellectual interests were allowed to participate fully, provided their interests were documented. Dr. Lynn Bailey, a professor at the University of Georgia, declared her research interests in folate metabolism and its impact on maternal and child health. Dr. Anne Molloy, from Trinity College Dublin, declared her involvement in research on folate and vitamin B12 metabolism, including genetic polymorphisms related to NTDs. Dr. Christine Pfeiffer, Chief of the Nutritional Biomarkers Branch at the CDC, contributed her expertise in folate and B-vitamin methodologies. Dr. Irma Silva-Zolezzi, employed by Nestlé Research Center, provided background information but did not participate in decision-making due to her affiliation with a commercial organization. The guideline is scheduled for review in 2024. WHO’s Department of Nutrition for Health and Development will coordinate the update, following formal procedures outlined in the WHO handbook for guideline development. WHO welcomes suggestions for additional questions to evaluate during the review process.
